_README: Adjudicated QA verdicts, so a reviewed episode stays reviewed.
qa_check.py regenerates QA_CHECKLIST.md from scratch on every run, which means
its checkboxes cannot hold review state -- tick one and the next run erases it.
Without this file, every session re-discovers and re-investigates the same
already-adjudicated episodes. That is what kept the flagged count stuck at
14-16 while real work was being done.
Keys are episode slugs. Under each, a signature name maps to a verdict.
Signature names match the `signature` argument in qa_check.py's issue() calls:
wall-of-text, drift, content-loss, duplicates, backward-jump, truncated,
coverage, round-timestamps, weak-model, language, split-timestamp,
leaked-reasoning, repetition-loop, short-loop, missing-file
verdict: "benign" moves the issue out of the flagged list into a separate
'Reviewed, judged benign' section. Any other verdict (or no entry) leaves it
flagged. Always record a reason and a date -- a suppression with no rationale
is worse than no suppression.
Re-flag by deleting the entry. If an episode is reprocessed and its content
changes, delete its entries so the new output gets judged fresh.
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28 -- the wall-of-text waivers on ep41/ep43/ep44/ep58, and ep44's
coverage waiver. All rested on one claim: 'the giant block carries a single speaker
label, so it is one real long monologue.' That is circular. A collapsed diarization
cluster produces exactly one label across the whole block, so the label count cannot
witness its own correctness. Reading those blocks found real co-host turns inside
them (ep58 'Devil's advocate sikit, YB'; ep43 'Kau rakyat jelata biasa?' answered by
'Saya rakyat jelita biasa lah'). The size trigger now lives in the separate
'oversized-block' signature, which does not consult the label count.
Waiving an issue needs evidence INDEPENDENT of the artefact under suspicion. Audio,
or dialogue content, or the roster -- not the label whose correctness is the question.
